table_title: List the 13 numbered permanent NATO Secretaries General with completed terms 1952-2024 (excluding incumbent Mark Rutte 2024-present and all 3 acting SG rows: Sergio Balanzino in 1994 and 1995 + Alessandro Minuto-Rizzo in 2003-2004), with the term start year, term end year, and the Secretary General's birth country derived from the per-person Wikipedia article's 'Born' field using the modern-sovereign-country-of-birthplace normalization rule.
db_analog: SELECT secretary_general, term_start_year, term_end_year, birth_country FROM nato_secretaries_general_with_birth_country WHERE is_numbered_permanent_officeholder = TRUE AND term_end_year IS NOT NULL AND term_end_year != 'Incumbent' ORDER BY term_start_year
temporal_note: Wikipedia 'Secretary General of NATO' master article (officeholders table) + 13 per-person Wikipedia articles, accessed 2026-05-16. Universe is the 13 numbered permanent NATO Secretaries General with completed terms 1952-2024 per the master article's officeholders table — Hastings Ismay (1952-1957) through Jens Stoltenberg (2014-2024). Two mechanical exclusions are applied to the master table: (a) incumbent Mark Rutte (since 1 October 2024; Term End Year = 'Incumbent' marker in master) is excluded because his term is not completed; (b) all 3 acting SG rows are excluded per the audit-recommended 'numbered permanent SG row' rule — Sergio Balanzino served as Acting SG twice (between Wörner's death July 1994 and Claes's appointment October 1994; then between Claes's resignation October 1995 and Solana's appointment December 1995), and Alessandro Minuto-Rizzo served as Acting SG between Robertson's departure 17 December 2003 and de Hoop Scheffer's appointment 1 January 2004 (a brief ~2-week interregnum). The master table marks acting rows with '–' rather than numbered officeholder rows, providing a clean mechanical filter. Per-row cells: Secretary-General is taken from each per-person Wikipedia article's canonical title — for peerage holders the full peerage name is used ('Hastings Ismay, 1st Baron Ismay'; 'Peter Carington, 6th Baron Carrington'; 'George Robertson, Baron Robertson of Port Ellen') per the audit-recommended per-person-article-title rule rather than common-display-shortened forms. Term Start Year and Term End Year are integer years extracted from the master table's full-date entries (e.g., '24 March 1952' → 1952 for Ismay Term Start; '1 October 2024' → 2024 for Stoltenberg Term End). Birth Country is the modern sovereign country containing the birthplace per the per-person Wikipedia article's 'Born' field — IMPORTANT: this is birth country NOT nationality or country-of-political-career; Hastings Ismay born Naini Tal, British India (1887) → 'India' (modern sovereign country) NOT 'United Kingdom' (his career country). The 13-row universe is stable on a multi-year horizon: completed-term SGs won't change retroactively; new rows would be added when Rutte's term ends (anticipated 2028).
_extraction_notes: Original instance SATURATING `implicit_join` at 8/8 — NINTH CATEGORY TO FULLY CLEAR after multi_attribute_projection 8/8, set_operation 8/8, set_filter 5/5, causal 5/5, factual_lookup 6/5 over-target, top_k 6/5 over-target, multi_hop 5/5, qualitative 5/5. Source plan: Tier B Wikipedia, source_count = 14 — 1 master 'Secretary General of NATO' Wikipedia article + 13 per-person Wikipedia articles (1 per SG). The pre-staging audit design review (1 round) confirmed the design is basically sound and surfaced 2 required fixes applied in cycle-0: (1) Acting SG exclusion must include ALL 3 acting rows (Sergio Balanzino twice + Alessandro Minuto-Rizzo once), not just Balanzino as initially proposed; the master table marks acting rows with '–' rather than numbered officeholder rows, providing a clean mechanical filter. (2) Name normalization uses per-person Wikipedia article titles (e.g., 'Hastings Ismay, 1st Baron Ismay' not 'Hastings Ismay' or 'Lord Ismay'; 'Peter Carington, 6th Baron Carrington' not 'Lord Carrington'; 'George Robertson, Baron Robertson of Port Ellen' not 'George Robertson') per the audit-recommended exact-provenance rule. Pipeline: (1) fetch the cited NATO Secretary General Wikipedia article HTML and extract the officeholders table rows for the 13 numbered permanent SGs with completed terms (filtering out incumbent Rutte and the 3 acting SG rows); (2) for each row, take Secretary-General name verbatim from the per-person Wikipedia article's canonical title, Term Start Year and Term End Year as integer years from the master table's full-date entries; (3) for each per-person article, extract Birth Country from the 'Born' field's geographic location using the modern-sovereign-country normalization rule (Ismay born Naini Tal, British India → 'India' modern sovereign country, NOT 'United Kingdom' career country). Result: 13 rows × 4 columns, single PK on Secretary-General, 0 duplicates. Birth Country distribution (9 distinct values): Netherlands 3 (Stikker, Luns, de Hoop Scheffer), United Kingdom 2 (Carrington, Robertson), Belgium 2 (Spaak, Claes), India 1 (Ismay — born British India 1887), Italy 1 (Brosio), Germany 1 (Wörner — born Stuttgart, Germany per his Wikipedia article's Born field), Spain 1 (Solana), Denmark 1 (Rasmussen), Norway 1 (Stoltenberg). Confidence gradient: very-LLM-knowable cells include canonical NATO SGs (Stoltenberg 2014-2024 Norway, Solana 1995-1999 Spain, Rasmussen 2009-2014 Denmark); mid-difficulty cells include the well-known Cold War / post-Cold War SGs (Carrington 1984-1988 UK, Wörner 1988-1994 Germany, Claes 1994-1995 Belgium); harder calibration cells include the early Cold War SGs (Ismay 1952-1957 India, Spaak 1957-1961 Belgium, Stikker 1961-1964 Netherlands, Brosio 1964-1971 Italy, Luns 1971-1984 Netherlands) and the Ismay-India edge case (born British India per modern-sovereign-country rule; this is the most-likely LLM-error case where the answer might be 'United Kingdom' under nationality-not-birth-country interpretation). The implicit-join cell (Birth Country) tests per-person article knowledge that requires looking up the SG's biography; this is DIFFERENT from the NATO master table's 'Country of origin' column (which would give nationality / political-career country) — the column-name distinction (Birth Country) is intentional to make the implicit join non-redundant. Implicit-join structure: master NATO article gives (Secretary-General, Term Start Year, Term End Year); per-person articles supply Birth Country — a clean single-master-multiple-per-entity implicit join matching the precedent set by nato_accessions_1999_2024_capitals (master gives Country+Year; per-country article gives Capital), notable_works_of_recent_nobel_literature_laureates, landmark_us_supreme_court_decisions_by_chief_justice, booker_prize_for_fiction_winners_2000_2024, and pulitzer_prize_for_fiction_winners_2000_2024.
